title: Harbor handoff: caretaker summary and follow-ups
content:
Shift: 03/07/2029 23:00-07:00 PT (Harbor bridge)
Owners (this handoff): Maya Gupta (primary), Liam O'Connor (secondary)
Summary: During the 23:40 UTC canary rollout of model-serving v1.12 we observed repeated autoscaler thrash in the eu-west pool that led to elevated 502/504s for long-sequence (>2048) inference requests. Root cause appears to be a memory-growth regression in the new allocator path introduced in the canary image; this caused nodes to hit OOMBackground and trigger frequent kubelet restarts and evictions.

Immediate impact observed:
- 23:42-00:20 UTC: p95 latency for text-generation (long seq) increased from 220ms -> 1.2s for eu-west customers; error rate rose to ~6% (baseline 0.2%).
- Autoscaler oscillation: 3 scale-up -> immediate OOMs -> node restart -> scale down -> repeat (avg 6 cycles over 40 minutes).
- No data plane compromise for non-long-seq traffic (short seq and embeddings remained stable).

Actions taken during shift:
1) 23:45 UTC: Rolled back canary image to v1.11 via rollout abort (k8s rollout undo) — mitigated immediate new failures.
2) 23:50 UTC: Manually cordoned 2 most-affected nodes to stop scheduling long-running requests; swapped traffic to healthy nodes in eu-west-b pool.
3) 00:05 UTC: Opened P0 Jira SRE-4821 and added heap profiles and kubelet logs.
4) 00:22 UTC: Increased short-term HPA stabilization window from 30s -> 120s to reduce autoscaler sensitivity (temp measure).
5) 00:45 UTC: Reapplied conservative pod memory requests on dedicated-serving daemonset to reduce eviction churn.

Observed during follow-ups:
- Heap profiles from 2 canary pods show steady growth in native allocator region after ~600s of runtime with sequences >2048.
- GC metrics and jemalloc stats indicate new code path is allocating many small arenas and not releasing them back to OS.
- Post-rollback traffic returned to baseline by 00:50 UTC; error rates back to ~0.25% by 01:10 UTC.

Open items for next shift / owners:
- SRE-4821 (Maya) - Attach annotated heap profiles (done), collect additional profiles for mid-sized sequences (Assigned: Priya) - due 2029-03-09.
- ENG-SERVE-1193 (Eng: Diego) - Reproduce locally with load generator and the v1.12 image; add guardrail to allocator initialization if leak reproduced - due 2029-03-10.
- Runbook change (Maya) - Add explicit canary memory smoke test for sequences 2k-8k in the preflight checklist. Draft below; review requested.
- Monitor tweak (Liam) - Add alert: "eu-west-serving: sustained pod mem RSS growth > 30% in 10m for canary label" (severity P2) - due 2029-03-09.

Runbook draft (quick patch to harbor runbook):
- Canary preflight step: "memory-smoke-longseq" test (6m) — spin 5 pods of canary image against synthetic long-seq workload (seq lengths: 2048, 4096, 8192) at 10 rps per pod; measure RSS and arena growth. Fail and abort rollout if median RSS increase > 25% or ephemeral OOM observed.
- Autoscaler stabilization guidance: set HPA stabilizationWindowSeconds=120 for serving pools during canary windows, revert after 1 hour if stable.
- Eviction mitigation: if autoscaler thrash observed -> cordon affected nodes, patch deployment to reduce memory request by 10% and roll out next; notify infra immediately.

Notes to oncoming shift:
- Keep SRE-4821 ticket front-and-center. Slack thread #sre-harbor-incident started at 23:41 UTC (link pinned in ticket).
- If canary re-rollout is attempted, require mandatory approval from oncall+serving-owner; do not allow automated promotion until allocator regression is resolved.
- Dashboard links: Serving-eu-west-pod-mem (shortlink: rbwd.co/srv-eu-mem), Autoscaler-loops (rbwd.co/auto-loops).

Post-incident retrospective items (suggested):
- Add canary long-seq synthetic suite to CI (fast, nightly) to catch allocator regressions earlier.
- Consider making the allocator opt-in behind a feature flag with telemetry that surfaces arena churn.
- Re-evaluate canary scaling policy (current quick promotion seems to amplify transient regressions).

Changelog (what I changed in runbook during handoff):
- Added "memory-smoke-longseq" checklist entry (draft) and shortlink to heap profile collection snippet.
- Temporary HPA stabilization recommendation appended to critical-response section.

Slack & comms:
- Customer notice: Notified S&M and CS at 00:05 UTC; suggested message drafted in #cs-product-alerts (staged, not sent).
- Engineers notified: Diego and serving-oncall looped in; Diego started local repro at 01:30 UTC.

If you take over: first tasks = 1) confirm SRE-4821 latest attachments, 2) run the heap profile analysis script in the ticket, 3) ensure the canary preflight test is added to the CI draft branch PR (ops-config PR/256).

Signature: Maya G. (oncall - Harbor bridge)
